alg-na-romberg-trapezoid-table:
## Definition

Input a real function $f$ on a nondegenerate closed interval $[a,b]$ and an integer $L\ge0$. The output is the finite triangular table $(R_{\ell,j})_{0\le j\le\ell\le L}$ and its top entry $R_{L,L}$.

1. For each $\ell=0,\ldots,L$, set $N_\ell=2^\ell$, $h_\ell=(b-a)/N_\ell$, and $R_{\ell,0}=T_{N_\ell}(f)$ using the composite trapezoidal value $T_N$ of [[def-composite-trapezoidal-rule]].
2. For $j=1,\ldots,L$, and then for each $\ell=j,\ldots,L$, set
$$R_{\ell,j}:=R_{\ell,j-1}+\frac{R_{\ell,j-1}-R_{\ell-1,j-1}}{4^j-1}.$$

All denominators are positive because $j\ge1$. This definition returns only the stated finite table; it makes no accuracy claim for nonsmooth inputs or finite-precision arithmetic.
def-na-bernoulli-polynomials:
## Definition

Define polynomials $B_m\in\mathbb R[X]$ recursively. Put $B_0(X)=1$. If $m\ge1$ and $B_{m-1}(X)=\sum_{q=0}^{m-1}\beta_{m-1,q}X^q$, set
$$B_m(X):=m\sum_{q=0}^{m-1}\beta_{m-1,q}\left(\frac{X^{q+1}}{q+1}-\frac{1}{(q+1)(q+2)}\right).$$
Natural numbers in real denominators mean their canonical real images from [[def-canonical-natural]]; these images are positive by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and therefore invertible in $\mathbb R$ by [[thm-reals-field]]. Every sum is finite. Write $B_m:=B_m(0)$ for the Bernoulli number of index $m$.
def-na-clenshaw-curtis-dct-i:
## Definition

Let $n\ge1$ be an integer and let $y=(y_0,\ldots,y_n)\in\mathbb R^{n+1}$. The type-I discrete cosine transform, in the Lobatto convention used here, is the vector $X=(X_0,\ldots,X_n)$ defined by
$$X_k:=y_0+(-1)^k y_n+2\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}y_j\cos\!\left(\frac{jk\pi}{n}\right),\qquad 0\le k\le n.$$
The sum is the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]] and is empty when $n=1$. The data $y_j$ are ordered from the right endpoint toward the left endpoint at nodes $\cos(j\pi/n)$. This definition fixes the unnormalised DCT-I convention; the transform is not defined at $n=0$.
def-na-closed-newton-cotes-eight-panel-r:
## Definition

For $j=0,\ldots,8$, set $x_j=-1+j/4$ and
$$w_j:=\frac{1}{14175}(989,5888,-928,10496,-4540,10496,-928,5888,989)_j.$$
For any real-valued function $f$ on $[-1,1]$, define the closed nine-node rule
$$Q_8(f):=\sum_{j=0}^{8}w_j f(x_j),$$
where the sum is finite. The nodes are equally spaced and include both endpoints; the subsequent weight and exactness lemma verifies that these coefficients are the integrated Lagrange-cardinal weights.
def-na-peano-kernel:
## Definition

Let $a<b$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_s\in[a,b]$ be a finite indexed list (repetitions are allowed), and let $w_1,\ldots,w_s\in\mathbb R$. For every Riemann-integrable $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$, define the quadrature value and residual by
$$Q(f):=\sum_{i=1}^{s}w_i f(x_i),\qquad L(f):=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx-Q(f).$$
For an integer $r\ge1$, say that $Q$ is exact through degree $r-1$ if $L(p)=0$ for every real polynomial $p$ of degree at most $r-1$. For $t\in[a,b]$ define
$$g_{r,t}(x):=\begin{cases}\dfrac{(x-t)^{r-1}}{(r-1)!},&x>t,\\0,&x\le t,\end{cases}\qquad K_r(t):=L(g_{r,t}).$$
For $r=1$, this means $g_{1,t}(x)=1$ when $x>t$ and $0$ otherwise; it is Riemann-integrable, and the values of $K_1$ at the finitely many quadrature nodes do not affect any integral of the kernel. For $r\ge2$, $g_{r,t}$ is continuous in $x$.
lem-na-chebyshev-degree-bound-from-recur:
## Statement

For every integer $n\ge0$, the coefficient list of the first-kind Chebyshev polynomial $T_n$ from [[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]] has no nonzero coefficient above index $n$. In particular, $\deg T_n\le n$.
lem-na-chebyshev-recurrence-angle-identi:
## Statement

For every integer $n\ge0$ and every real $\theta$, the first-kind Chebyshev polynomial from [[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]] satisfies
$$T_n(\cos\theta)=\cos(n\theta).$$
lem-na-bernoulli-polynomial-identities:
## Statement

For the polynomials of [[def-na-bernoulli-polynomials]] and every integer $m\ge1$,
$$B'_m(x)=mB_{m-1}(x),\qquad \int_0^1 B_m(x)\,dx=0.$$
In particular, $B_0(x)=1$ and $B_1(x)=x-\tfrac12$.
Consequently $B_m(1)=B_m(0)$ for $m\ge2$. The reflection identity $B_m(1-x)=(-1)^mB_m(x)$ holds for every $m\ge0$, so $B_m(0)=0$ for odd $m\ge3$. Each $B_m$ is bounded on $[0,1]$.
lem-na-chebyshev-integral-moments:
## Statement

For every integer $k\ge0$, let $\mu_k:=\int_{-1}^{1}T_k(x)\,dx$, where $T_k$ is the first-kind Chebyshev polynomial. Then
$$\mu_k=\begin{cases}2,&k=0,\\0,&k\text{ odd},\\[2pt]\dfrac{2}{1-k^2},&k\ge2\text{ even}.\end{cases}$$
Equivalently, $\mu_{2r}=2/(1-4r^2)$ for every integer $r\ge0$.
lem-na-clenshaw-curtis-dct-i-orthogonali:
## Statement

For $n\ge1$ and integers $0\le k,\ell\le n$, define
$$S_{k\ell}:=\frac12\cos(0)+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\cos\!\left(\frac{jk\pi}{n}\right)\cos\!\left(\frac{j\ell\pi}{n}\right)+\frac12(-1)^{k+\ell}.$$
Then $S_{k\ell}=n$ when $k=\ell=0$ or $k=\ell=n$, $S_{k\ell}=n/2$ when $k=\ell$ is strictly between $0$ and $n$, and $S_{k\ell}=0$ when $k\ne\ell$. The half-endpoint convention is the one used by the DCT-I of [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-dct-i]].
thm-na-peano-kernel-remainder-and-bound:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, let $x_1,\ldots,x_s\in[a,b]$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_s\in\mathbb R$ define the finite quadrature $Q$ and residual $L$ of [[def-na-peano-kernel]], and let $r\ge1$ be an integer. Assume $Q$ is exact for every polynomial of degree at most $r-1$, and let $f\in C^r([a,b])$. For the kernel $K_r(t)=L(g_{r,t})$ of [[def-na-peano-kernel]],
$$L(f)=\int_a^b K_r(t)f^{(r)}(t)\,dt,\qquad |L(f)|\le \left(\int_a^b|K_r(t)|\,dt\right)\|f^{(r)}\|_\infty.$$
thm-na-euler-maclaurin-composite-trapezo:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, let $N\ge1$ and $p\ge1$ be integers, put $h=(b-a)/N$ and $x_i=a+ih$, and let $f\in C^{2p}([a,b])$ in the sense of [[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]]. Write $B_m(x)$ for [[def-na-bernoulli-polynomials]] and $B_m:=B_m(0)$. For $u_i(x):=(x-x_i)/h$ on $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$, the composite trapezoidal value $T_N(f)$ of [[def-composite-trapezoidal-rule]] satisfies
$$T_N(f)=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx+\sum_{r=1}^{p}\frac{B_{2r}h^{2r}}{(2r)!}\bigl(f^{(2r-1)}(b)-f^{(2r-1)}(a)\bigr)-\frac{h^{2p}}{(2p)!}\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\int_{x_i}^{x_{i+1}}B_{2p}(u_i(x))f^{(2p)}(x)\,dx.$$
In particular, with $M_{2p}:=\max_{0\le u\le1}|B_{2p}(u)|$, the absolute value of the final remainder is at most $(b-a)M_{2p}h^{2p}\|f^{(2p)}\|_\infty/(2p)!$.
cor-na-composite-trapezoid-even-power-ex:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, let $j\ge1$ be an integer, and let $f\in C^{2j+2}([a,b])$. For $N\ge1$ set $h=(b-a)/N$, $I=\int_a^b f$, and
$$c_r:=\frac{B_{2r}}{(2r)!}\bigl(f^{(2r-1)}(b)-f^{(2r-1)}(a)\bigr),\qquad 1\le r\le j+1,$$
using the Bernoulli numbers of [[def-na-bernoulli-polynomials]]. Then
$$T_N(f)=I+\sum_{r=1}^{j}c_rh^{2r}+\varepsilon_N,\qquad |\varepsilon_N|\le C_jh^{2j+2},$$
where the level-independent finite constant
$$C_j:=|c_{j+1}|+\frac{(b-a)M_{2j+2}}{(2j+2)!}\|f^{(2j+2)}\|_\infty,\qquad M_{2j+2}:=\max_{0\le u\le1}|B_{2j+2}(u)|,$$
does not depend on $N$. Thus the remainder bound is uniform over every set of dyadic levels.
lem-na-closed-newton-cotes-eight-panel-w:
## Statement

For the nodes $x_j=-1+j/4$ and rule $Q_8$ of [[def-na-closed-newton-cotes-eight-panel-rule]], the weights are the integrals of the degree-eight Lagrange cardinal polynomials. The rule is exact for every polynomial of degree at most $9$.
thm-na-romberg-even-power-cancellation:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, let $m\ge1$ and $L\ge m$ be integers, and let $f\in C^{2m+2}([a,b])$. Write $h_\ell=(b-a)2^{-\ell}$ and let $(R_{\ell,j})$ be the table from [[alg-na-romberg-trapezoid-table]]. If the trapezoid expansion has coefficients $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ as in [[cor-na-composite-trapezoid-even-power-expansion]], then the recurrence cancels all first $m$ even powers and there is a finite $C_{m,L}$ such that
$$|R_{L,m}-\int_a^b f(x)\,dx|\le C_{m,L}h_L^{2m+2}.$$
No error-order conclusion is made from a ratio of observed consecutive trapezoid errors.
cor-na-closed-newton-cotes-eight-panel-p:
## Statement

If $f\in C^{10}[-1,1]$, then the rule $Q_8$ of [[def-na-closed-newton-cotes-eight-panel-rule]] satisfies
$$\left|\int_{-1}^1f(x)\,dx-Q_8(f)\right|\le\left(\int_{-1}^1|K_{10}(t)|\,dt\right)\|f^{(10)}\|_\infty,$$
where
$$K_{10}(t)=\frac{(1-t)^{10}}{10!}-\sum_{j=0}^8w_j\frac{(x_j-t)_+^9}{9!},\qquad x_j=-1+j/4,$$
and $u_+:=\max(u,0)$.
thm-na-clenshaw-curtis-interpolation-coe:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and let $g\in C[-1,1]$. Put $y_j=g(\cos(j\pi/n))$ for $0\le j\le n$, and let $X_k$ be the DCT-I of [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-dct-i]]. Define
$$a_0:=\frac{X_0}{2n},\qquad a_n:=\frac{X_n}{2n},\qquad a_k:=\frac{X_k}{n}\quad(1\le k<n).$$
Then $p_n(t):=\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_kT_k(t)$ is the unique polynomial of degree at most $n$ interpolating $g$ at the Chebyshev–Lobatto nodes $\cos(j\pi/n)$; in particular $p_n=I_n^L g$ in the convention of [[def-best-uniform-polynomial-approximation-error-and-chebyshev-interpolants]].
def-na-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature:
## Definition

Let $a<b$, $m=(a+b)/2$, $d=(b-a)/2$, and $f\in C[a,b]$. For $n\ge1$, set $g(t):=f(m+dt)$ on $[-1,1]$, let $y_j=g(\cos(j\pi/n))$, and form $a_0,\ldots,a_n$ from the DCT-I coefficients in [[thm-na-clenshaw-curtis-interpolation-coefficients]]. With the Chebyshev moments $\mu_k$ of [[lem-na-chebyshev-integral-moments]], define
$$Q_{n,[a,b]}(f):=d\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_k\mu_k.$$
For $n=0$, define instead
$$Q_{0,[a,b]}(f):=(b-a)f(m),$$
the midpoint rule. This is the explicit endpoint and zero-degree convention for Clenshaw–Curtis quadrature. The sums and coefficients are exact real quantities; finite-precision evaluation is a separate algorithm.
thm-na-clenshaw-curtis-exactness-and-nea:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, $n\ge0$, and $f\in C[a,b]$. Put $m=(a+b)/2$, $d=(b-a)/2$, and $g(t)=f(m+dt)$ on $[-1,1]$. Let $E_n(g)$ and $\Lambda_n^L$ be the best uniform polynomial error and the Chebyshev–Lobatto interpolation norm from [[def-best-uniform-polynomial-approximation-error-and-chebyshev-interpolants]]. The rule $Q_{n,[a,b]}$ of [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature]] is exact for every polynomial of degree at most $n$, and
$$\left|\int_a^b f(x)\,dx-Q_{n,[a,b]}(f)\right|\le(b-a)(1+\Lambda_n^L)E_n(g).$$
Because affine pullback preserves the supremum norm and polynomial degree, $E_n(g)$ is also the best degree-$n$ uniform error of $f$ on $[a,b]$.
alg-na-computed-clenshaw-curtis-via-fast:
## Definition

Input real numbers $a<b$, an integer $n\ge0$, sampled values $y_0,\ldots,y_n$, and the phase/FFT controls for [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]]: a phase tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial phase precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, and a maximum radix-two recursion depth $d_{\max}\ge0$. For $n\ge1$, the samples are ordered as $y_j=f(m+d\cos(j\pi/n))$ with $m=(a+b)/2$ and $d=(b-a)/2$. The output is an approximate real quadrature value or the first status returned by the called DFT procedure.

1. If $n=0$, return $(b-a)y_0$, the midpoint convention of [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature]].
2. If $n\ge1$, form $z\in\mathbb R^{2n}$ by $z_j=y_j$ for $0\le j\le n$ and $z_{2n-j}=y_j$ for $1\le j<n$. This is the even extension $(y_0,\ldots,y_n,y_{n-1},\ldots,y_1)$. Call [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]] on $z$ with length $2n$ and the same controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$. If it returns a status instead of a vector, return that status.
3. Otherwise, take the real parts $X_k$ of output entries $0\le k\le n$, form the DCT-I coefficients $a_0=X_0/(2n)$, $a_n=X_n/(2n)$, and $a_k=X_k/n$ for $1\le k<n$ as in [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-dct-i]], and return $d\sum_{k=0}^n a_k\mu_k$ with the exact moments $\mu_k$ in [[def-na-clenshaw-curtis-quadrature]].

The postprocessing is exact real arithmetic applied to the approximate DFT output. The procedure makes no end-to-end floating-point error or stability claim; it only propagates the DFT routine's declared failure statuses.
